title: "Power vs. Endurance: Sprint vs. Distance Swimmers"
subtitle: "Examining physiological trade-offs between explosive speed and aerobic efficiency"
format:

    toc: true
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
---

```{r}
#| label: sprint-vs-distance
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5

library(tidyverse)

df <- read_csv("data/olympics.csv.gz", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(sport == "Swimming", year >= 1980, !is.na(height), !is.na(weight)) |>
  mutate(
    discipline = case_when(
      str_detect(event, "50 metres|100 metres Freestyle") ~ "Sprint (50m/100m)",
      str_detect(event, "400 metres|800 metres|1,500 metres Freestyle") ~ "Distance (400m+)",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    sex = if_else(sex == "M", "Men", "Women")
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(discipline))

medians <- df |>
  group_by(sex, discipline) |>
  summarize(height = median(height), weight = median(weight), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(df, aes(x = height, y = weight, color = discipline)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 1.6) +
  geom_point(
    data = medians,
    aes(x = height, y = weight, fill = discipline),
    size = 4,
    shape = 23,
    color = "black",
    stroke = 1.2
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~sex, scales = "free") +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  labs(
    title = "Physiological Profiles of Olympic Freestyle Swimmers (1980-2016)",
    subtitle = "Diamonds mark the median athlete in each event category",
    x = "Height (cm)",
    y = "Weight (kg)",
    color = "Discipline",
    fill = "Discipline"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Physical Trade-offs in the Pool

Freestyle events demand fundamentally different physical profiles depending on race distance:

- **Sprinters (50m & 100m)** rely on explosive power and upper-body leverage to overcome water resistance over short distances. As seen above, medalists and competitors in sprint events are both taller and noticeably heavier.
- **Distance swimmers (400m to 1,500m)** prioritize aerobic capacity and swimming efficiency. Carrying excess muscle mass increases drag and metabolic cost across a race lasting up to fifteen minutes, resulting in leaner, lighter body profiles.
